exercises.title: U6 听力·对话 Joining the Space Camp
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: Leo, have you seen the advertisement for the summer space camp?
Leo: Yes! They say you can try a real flight simulator there.
Mia: That sounds awesome. Do you think we are brave enough to join?
Leo: Of course. We only need to submit a short video about ourselves.
Mia: I'm a little nervous, but I really want to learn about astronomy.
Leo: Me too. My dream is to become an astronaut one day.
Mia: Then let's apply together this weekend.
Leo: Great idea. We can help each other write the video.
exercises.translation_cn: 米娅问里奥有没有看到暑期太空营的广告;里奥说能体验真正的飞行模拟器;米娅觉得很棒,但担心他们是否够勇敢;里奥说只需提交一段自我介绍的短视频;米娅有点紧张但很想学天文学;里奥的梦想是当宇航员;两人决定周末一起申请、互相帮忙拍视频。

questions.stem: What can people try at the space camp?
What do they need to submit to join?
How does Mia feel about joining?
What is Leo's dream?
options: To become an astronaut one day.

questions.stem: When do they decide to apply?

exercises.title: U6 听力·短文 The First Person in Space
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: In 1961, Yuri Gagarin became the first person to travel into space.
His flight lasted less than two hours, but it changed history.
Millions of people were amazed that a human could orbit the Earth.
His courage opened the door for many astronauts who came after him.
Today we still remember him as a hero of space exploration.
exercises.translation_cn: 1961年,尤里·加加林成为首位进入太空的人;他的飞行不到两个小时,却改变了历史;数百万人惊叹于人类竟能绕地球飞行;他的勇气为后来的许多宇航员打开了大门;今天我们仍把他当作太空探索的英雄铭记。

questions.stem: What did Yuri Gagarin become in 1961?
options: The first man on the Moon.
The first to build a rocket.
The first person to travel into space.

questions.stem: How long did his flight last?
Why were millions of people amazed?
options: A human could orbit the Earth.

questions.stem: What did his courage do for others?
options: It opened the door for later astronauts.

questions.stem: How is Gagarin remembered today?
options: As a hero of space exploration.

exercises.title: U6 听力·对话 Asking an Astronaut about Daily Life
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Student: Excuse me, what is the hardest part of living in space?
Astronaut: Even simple tasks become difficult without gravity.
Student: Really? Can you give me an example?
Astronaut: Yes. We have to strap ourselves down just to sleep safely.
Student: That sounds strange. How do you stay healthy up there?
Astronaut: We must exercise every day, or our muscles grow weak.
Student: What about eating? Is that difficult too?
Astronaut: A little. Salt and pepper come in liquid form, or they would float away.
exercises.translation_cn: 学生问宇航员在太空生活最难的是什么;宇航员说没有重力,连简单的事都变难;比如睡觉时得把自己绑住才安全;为保持健康必须每天锻炼,否则肌肉会变弱;吃东西也有点难,盐和胡椒做成液体,否则会漂走。

questions.stem: What becomes difficult without gravity?
What must astronauts do just to sleep safely?
Why do astronauts exercise every day?
options: So their muscles do not grow weak.

questions.stem: How do salt and pepper come in space?
Why are they in liquid form?

exercises.title: U6 听力·短文 How Astronauts Train
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Becoming an astronaut takes years of hard training.
Trainees learn to stay calm in a flight simulator that feels completely real.
They also practise moving in special pools that copy zero gravity.
Self-discipline is just as important as physical strength.
Only those who never give up are ready for a real mission.
exercises.translation_cn: 成为宇航员需要多年的艰苦训练;学员在逼真的飞行模拟器里学会保持冷静;他们还在模拟零重力的特殊水池中练习活动;自律和体力同样重要;只有从不放弃的人才准备好执行真正的任务。

questions.stem: How long does astronaut training take?
What does the flight simulator feel like?
What do the special pools copy?
What is just as important as physical strength?
Who is ready for a real mission?

exercises.title: U6 听力·对话 Is There Life Out There?
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Sophie: Do you think there is life on other planets, Eric?
Eric: There must be millions of planets like ours, so it seems likely.
Sophie: But we have found no clear evidence of it at all.
Eric: That's true. Some scientists call this puzzle the Fermi Paradox.
Sophie: If life exists, do you think it would look like us?
Eric: Maybe, maybe not. Evolution might take a very different path.
Sophie: I really hope we make contact one day.
Eric: So do I, but the distances in space are simply enormous.
exercises.translation_cn: 苏菲问埃里克是否相信外星有生命;埃里克说一定有数百万颗像地球的行星,所以似乎很可能;可苏菲说至今没有确凿证据;埃里克说这个谜被称作费米悖论;苏菲问外星生命会不会像人类;埃里克说也许像也许不像,进化可能走完全不同的路;两人都希望有朝一日能联系上,但太空距离实在太遥远。

questions.stem: Why does Eric think life is likely?
options: There must be millions of planets like ours.

questions.stem: What have they found no clear evidence of?
What do some scientists call this puzzle?
Why might alien life look different from us?
options: Evolution might take a different path.

questions.stem: What does Eric say makes contact hard?

exercises.title: U6 听力·短文 A Word about Courage
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is something to remember about exploring the unknown.
Real courage does not mean feeling no fear at all.
It means doing the right thing even when you are afraid.
The early astronauts knew the danger, yet they still climbed aboard.
Whenever you face a challenge, take a deep breath and keep going.
exercises.translation_cn: 关于探索未知,有一点值得记住:真正的勇气并不是毫无恐惧;而是即使害怕也去做对的事;早期的宇航员明知危险,却仍然登上飞船;每当你面对挑战,深吸一口气,继续前行。

questions.stem: What does real courage not mean?
What does courage really mean?
options: Doing the right thing even when afraid.

questions.stem: What did the early astronauts know?
What did they do despite the danger?
What should you do when you face a challenge?
options: Take a deep breath and keep going.
